messages.subject: Shiny file saving & loading
parts:
Hi all,
I have built an application that has an reactive input, and when the input changes, it calls a customized function X(), in which it saves a model to a RData file. 
My question is, if I have two different clients that visit my app from their machine, when they change the input, will that RData file be stored/loaded on/from server side or locally? 
If server side, then will it cause synchronizing issues? If client side, then will it automatically save to client's machine?

Here's some code for reference:

Server.R
server <- function(input,output,session){
  model <- reactive({
    modelRes<-NA
    
      setProgress(message = "Updating Model...")

      #Model is saved in "ValueMatrix.RData" in this function TopicModelTrain(), e.g., save(model, file = "ValueMatrix.RData")
      TopicModelTrain(isolate({input$sparsity}),isolate({input$TFIDFfilterLevel}),0.9,TRUE,input$topicNum,isolate({input$newdatatrain}),testingData,20,10)  

      load("ValueMatrix.RData")

        ......

    return(modelRes)
  })
  ......
}


topicmodelingTest.R

...if(!file.exists("trainedModel.RData"))return(FALSE)
    load("trainedModel.RData")

if(file.exists("ValueMatrix.RData"))
      load("ValueMatrix.RData")      # Matrix generated by training data is saved

.... Update Matrix based on testing data
save(Matrix,file = "ValueMatrix.RData")


An important reason of raising this question is that, the training data might or might not be changed, which means user could at some point train a model with new data, or still use the previous model if no new data is coming. 
We do not want to go through the training process every new session, because when original dataset is large, it might take a long time, and if no new data within a while, we could reuse the model if save to a file.  

Appreciate your help!

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Shiny file saving & loading
parts:
Yinghao,
Your question is more of a Shiny development question and probably should be posted to the shiny-discuss list.  That being said, I believe that you will need to think about how to save the file to a different name by user.  The alternative would be to keep the data in memory perhaps and then you wouldn't have to worry about any of that.  

-Tareef
